stories.title: Fed holds at 3.75–4.00%, two dissenters wanted a hike

sections.label: Decision
sections.text: The Fed held rates steady after hiking 25 basis points in September. Two of the 12 voters dissented, and both wanted another quarter-point hike. Chairman Kevin Warsh said future moves can't be determined yet. He also said one 2027 meeting and two 2028 meetings will focus on strategy, with no rate vote.

sections.label: Market read
sections.text: Stocks and long-term yields edged higher as Wall Street read Warsh as hesitant to hike aggressively. CME FedWatch still puts the odds of a December hike at 85%. WSJ reported oil above $115.

stories.title: Alphabet falls 10% on a rare miss while Microsoft rises on Azure

sections.label: Alphabet
sections.text: Alphabet missed on both revenue and earnings for the first time in nearly four years. Free cash flow was negative $9.07 billion, against an expected negative $2.70 billion. Long-term debt rose to $125.1 billion from $21.6 billion. Capex is expected to exceed $300 billion in 2027.

sections.label: Microsoft
sections.text: Microsoft rose 4% after hours. Azure grew 48%, and the company guided Azure growth to 49–50%, against a 45.1% consensus.

stories.title: Oracle jumps 11%, and a DoorDash–Instacart deal could come Thursday

sections.label: Movers
sections.text: Oracle rose 11% after forecasting $225 billion in fiscal 2030 revenue and capping new fundraising at $20 billion. Sources told CNBC that DoorDash could announce a deal for Instacart as early as Thursday. Reports value Instacart at about $17 billion. Wendy's jumped 15% on a $1.4 billion offer from Trian.
